title: 🌍 UNIT 6: SOLUTIONS TO ENVIRONMENTAL AND SUSTAINABILITY PROBLEMS
notes: Environmental problems affect ecosystems, economies and human well-being.

title: 🌫️ 6.1 ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS
notes:
Environmental problems are changes in the natural environment that negatively affect ecosystems and human well-being.

Major problems →
🔹 Pollution
🔹 Ozone depletion
🔹 Biodiversity loss
🔹 Deforestation
🔹 Land degradation
🔹 Water scarcity
🔹 Waste accumulation
🔹 Climate-related environmental changes

title: 🏭 6.1.1 POLLUTION
notes:
Pollution → introduction of harmful substances or forms of energy into the environment beyond its capacity to absorb or process them.

Major types →
💨 Air pollution
💧 Water pollution
🌱 Soil pollution
🔊 Noise pollution
☢️ Radioactive pollution

⭐ Pollution can damage ecosystems, reduce resource quality and threaten human health.

title: 💨 6.1.2 AIR POLLUTION
notes:
Air pollution → contamination of the atmosphere by harmful gases, particles or other substances.

Major pollutants →
🔹 Carbon monoxide (CO)
🔹 Sulfur dioxide (SO₂)
🔹 Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)
🔹 Volatile organic compounds (VOCs)
🔹 Particulate matter
🔹 Ground-level ozone

Major sources → vehicles + industries + fuel combustion + waste burning + household energy use.

title: 🌊 6.1.3 WATER POLLUTION
notes:
Water pollution → contamination that changes water quality and makes it harmful or unsuitable for intended uses.

Sources →
🔹 Domestic sewage
🔹 Industrial waste
🔹 Agricultural chemicals
🔹 Oil and other hazardous substances
🔹 Solid waste
🔹 Sediments

Effects → disease + ecosystem damage + reduced water quality + loss of aquatic life.

title: 🌱 6.1.4 SOIL & LAND DEGRADATION
notes:
Land degradation → decline in the productive and ecological quality of land.

Major causes →
🔹 Deforestation
🔹 Overgrazing
🔹 Unsustainable cultivation
🔹 Soil erosion
🔹 Poor irrigation practices
🔹 Mining
🔹 Urban expansion

Effects → reduced soil fertility + lower agricultural productivity + erosion + habitat loss + food insecurity.

title: 🌳 6.1.5 DEFORESTATION
notes:
Deforestation → removal or destruction of forests, often resulting in conversion of forest land to other uses.

Major causes →
🔹 Agricultural expansion
🔹 Fuelwood and charcoal demand
🔹 Settlement expansion
🔹 Commercial logging
🔹 Infrastructure development

Effects → soil erosion + biodiversity loss + habitat destruction + altered water cycles + increased carbon emissions.

title: 🦋 6.1.6 BIODIVERSITY LOSS
notes:
Biodiversity → variety of living organisms, genes and ecosystems.

Biodiversity loss → reduction in the variety or abundance of living organisms.

Major causes →
🔹 Habitat destruction
🔹 Deforestation
🔹 Pollution
🔹 Overexploitation
🔹 Invasive species
🔹 Climate change

⭐ Biodiversity supports food, medicine, ecosystem services and ecological stability.

title: 🌀 6.1.7 OZONE DEPLETION
notes:
Ozone layer → atmospheric layer containing high concentrations of ozone that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

Ozone depletion → thinning or reduction of stratospheric ozone.

Major ozone-depleting substances → chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and related chemicals.

Effects → increased ultraviolet radiation reaching Earth's surface, creating risks to human health, crops and ecosystems.

⭐ The Montreal Protocol is a major international agreement for controlling ozone-depleting substances.

title: ♻️ 6.1.8 WASTE POLLUTION
notes:
Waste pollution occurs when solid, liquid or hazardous wastes are improperly produced, handled, treated or disposed of.

Problems →
🔹 Soil and water contamination
🔹 Air pollution from burning
🔹 Disease risks
🔹 Habitat degradation
🔹 Blocked drainage systems
🔹 Plastic accumulation

⭐ Reduce → Reuse → Recycle → Recover → Dispose safely.

title: 🌱 6.2 THE CHALLENGE OF SUSTAINABILITY
notes:
Sustainability → meeting human needs while maintaining the capacity of natural and social systems to support future generations.

Major sustainability challenges →
🔹 Population growth
🔹 Urbanization
🔹 Poverty
🔹 Resource depletion
🔹 Water scarcity
🔹 Food insecurity
🔹 Waste and pollution
🔹 Biodiversity loss
🔹 Climate change

title: 👥 6.2.1 POPULATION GROWTH & SUSTAINABILITY
notes:
Population growth can increase demand for:

🌾 Food
💧 Water
🏠 Housing
⚡ Energy
🌳 Land and forests
🏥 Social services

If resource use is poorly managed → environmental degradation and pressure on infrastructure may increase.

⭐ Sustainable planning should balance population needs with available resources.

title: 🏙️ 6.2.2 URBANIZATION & SUSTAINABILITY
notes:
Rapid urbanization can create pressure on:

🔹 Housing
🔹 Transportation
🔹 Water supply
🔹 Sanitation
🔹 Waste management
🔹 Energy systems
🔹 Urban land

Sustainable urban development → efficient infrastructure + adequate services + planned land use + environmental protection.

title: 💧 6.2.3 WATER SCARCITY
notes:
Water scarcity → insufficient available water to satisfy human and environmental needs.

Causes →
🔹 Population growth
🔹 Increasing demand
🔹 Pollution
🔹 Drought
🔹 Overuse of water resources
🔹 Poor management
🔹 Climate variability

Solutions → efficient irrigation + water conservation + pollution control + rainwater harvesting + watershed protection.

title: 🌾 6.2.4 SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE
notes:
Sustainable agriculture → farming that maintains productivity while conserving soil, water and biodiversity.

Practices →
🔹 Crop rotation
🔹 Soil conservation
🔹 Terracing
🔹 Agroforestry
🔹 Integrated pest management
🔹 Efficient irrigation
🔹 Organic matter management
🔹 Conservation of local crop varieties

⭐ Goal → productive agriculture without destroying the resource base.

title: ⚡ 6.2.5 RENEWABLE ENERGY
notes:
Renewable energy → energy obtained from resources that are naturally replenished.

Examples →
☀️ Solar
💨 Wind
💧 Hydropower
🌋 Geothermal
🌿 Biomass

Advantages → reduces dependence on finite fuels + can reduce greenhouse-gas emissions + supports long-term energy security.

title: 📚 6.3 ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION
notes:
Environmental education → learning process that develops environmental awareness, knowledge, skills, attitudes and responsible behavior.

⭐ Main purpose → help people understand environmental problems and participate in solving them.

title: 🎯 6.3.1 OBJECTIVES OF ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION
notes:
Environmental education aims to develop:

🧠 Awareness → understanding environmental issues.

📚 Knowledge → understanding ecosystems and environmental processes.

🛠️ Skills → ability to identify and solve environmental problems.

❤️ Attitudes → concern and responsibility toward the environment.

🤝 Participation → active involvement in environmental protection.

⭐ Awareness → Knowledge → Skills → Attitudes → Action.

title: 🏫 6.3.2 ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION IN PRACTICE
notes:
Environmental education can occur through:

🔹 Schools and environmental clubs.
🔹 Community programs.
🔹 Public awareness campaigns.
🔹 Fieldwork and environmental projects.
🔹 Media and communication.
🔹 Conservation activities.

⭐ Practical participation turns environmental knowledge into responsible action.

title: 🌍 6.4 ENVIRONMENTAL MOVEMENTS
notes:
Environmental movements → organized efforts by individuals and groups to protect the environment and influence environmental policies and practices.

They address issues such as → pollution + conservation + climate change + resource use + biodiversity + environmental justice.

title: 🕰️ 6.4.1 DEVELOPMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL MOVEMENTS
notes:
Environmental movements developed as awareness of environmental degradation increased.

🔹 Early conservation → protection of forests, wildlife and natural areas.

🔹 Modern environmentalism → expanded toward pollution, environmental health and resource management.

🔹 Global environmental movement → increasingly connects environmental protection with social and economic issues.

⭐ Environmental movements influence public awareness, policies and collective action.

title: 🌿 6.4.2 TYPES OF ENVIRONMENTAL MOVEMENTS
notes:
🔹 Free-market environmentalism → emphasizes market mechanisms and property rights as tools for environmental protection.

🔹 Bright Green environmentalism → focuses on technology, innovation and practical solutions.

🔹 Light/Dark environmentalism → represents differing approaches and levels of emphasis in responding to environmental problems.

🔹 Popular environmentalism → grassroots movements based on community concerns and environmental justice.

title: ✊ 6.4.3 ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVISM
notes:
Environmental activism may involve:

🔹 Public awareness campaigns.
🔹 Environmental clubs and organizations.
🔹 Community conservation.
🔹 Policy advocacy.
🔹 Peaceful demonstrations.
🔹 Restoration and clean-up activities.
🔹 Protection of threatened ecosystems.

⭐ Effective activism connects public participation with practical environmental solutions.

title: 🌾 6.5 ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY INDIGENOUS PRACTICES
notes:
Indigenous knowledge → local, traditional knowledge developed through long-term interaction with a particular environment.

Key characteristics →
🔹 Local and place-based.
🔹 Passed through generations.
🔹 Often transmitted orally or through demonstration.
🔹 Developed through practical experience and trial and error.
🔹 Community-based and widely shared.
🔹 Dynamic and adaptable.

⭐ Indigenous knowledge can contribute to sustainable environmental management.

title: ⛰️ 6.5.1 TERRACING & SOIL CONSERVATION
notes:
Terracing → shaping sloping land into step-like surfaces to reduce runoff and soil erosion.

Benefits →
🔹 Reduces soil loss.
🔹 Slows water flow.
🔹 Conserves soil moisture.
🔹 Improves cultivation on slopes.
🔹 Helps maintain land productivity.

⭐ Traditional soil-conservation practices can be valuable when adapted to local environmental conditions.

title: 💧 6.5.2 INDIGENOUS WATER MANAGEMENT
notes:
Traditional communities use locally developed knowledge to manage water resources.

Practices can include:
🔹 Protecting springs and water sources.
🔹 Community rules for water access.
🔹 Traditional irrigation methods.
🔹 Watershed and vegetation protection.
🔹 Shared management of scarce water resources.

⭐ Community-based management can improve conservation and equitable access.

title: 🌳 6.5.3 INDIGENOUS ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT
notes:
Traditional environmental practices can support ecosystem conservation through:

🔹 Protection of sacred or culturally important areas.
🔹 Controlled use of forests and vegetation.
🔹 Seasonal resource-use practices.
🔹 Community rules governing natural resources.
🔹 Protection of biodiversity.

⭐ Local environmental knowledge can complement scientific approaches to conservation.

title: 🌿 6.5.4 INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE & MEDICINAL PLANTS
notes:
Traditional communities possess knowledge of locally available plants and their uses.

🔹 Folk medicinal knowledge can contribute to health practices.
🔹 Knowledge is commonly transferred between generations.
🔹 Sustainable harvesting helps preserve useful plant species.

⚠️ Traditional knowledge should be documented and conserved while ensuring responsible and sustainable resource use.

title: 🇪🇹 6.5.5 ETHIOPIAN INDIGENOUS ENVIRONMENTAL PRACTICES
notes:
Examples of environmentally beneficial indigenous practices in Ethiopia include:

🔹 Terracing and soil conservation.
🔹 Traditional water-management practices.
🔹 Community-based ecosystem management.
🔹 Sustainable use of vegetation and forest resources.
🔹 Traditional knowledge of medicinal plants.
🔹 Local rules for managing communal resources.

⭐ Ethiopian indigenous knowledge provides locally adapted approaches to environmental management.

title: 🧠 UNIT 6 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
🌫️ Pollution → harmful contamination of the environment.

🌀 Ozone depletion → reduction of protective stratospheric ozone.

🦋 Biodiversity loss → reduction in biological variety.

🌳 Deforestation → removal of forest cover.

🌱 Sustainability → meeting present needs while maintaining future capacity.

📚 Environmental education → develops awareness, knowledge, skills, attitudes and participation.

🌍 Environmental movement → organized action to protect the environment.

🌾 Indigenous knowledge → local knowledge developed through long-term community experience.

⭐ Sustainability challenge → requires changes in how people produce, consume and manage resources.
